title: 38_143685_box_Incident_Summaries_173-233
what_is_it: A collection of US military incident summary reports (check-list format) documenting multiple unidentified flying object sightings from 1948.
interpretation_warnings: OCR quality is poor throughout, making many details difficult to read with certainty; some quoted text may contain transcription errors
Multiple incidents show contradictory testimony between co-witnesses observing the same event (Incidents 175/175a and 176/176a), undermining reliability
Several witnesses were assessed as unreliable by investigators (Incidents 177, 179, 189)
At least one incident (187) was conclusively identified as the planet Venus
Incident 180 has no report filed yet ('No report on this as yet')
Observer distance and size estimates were found faulty in at least one case (Incident 186)
The document covers incidents from 1947-1948; some details may reflect the limited observational and recording technology of the era
Moderate redaction and document degradation obscure some fields in the standardized check-lists

verifiable_claims.claim: A cone-shaped flaming object was observed in Ascension Parish, LA on 1 Oct 1948 traveling east at approximately 200 MPH at 1500-2000 ft altitude
verifiable_claims.source_quote: resembled an ice cream cone traveling east with the larger end in front... appeared to be about 3/4 miles away and at an elevation of approximately 2500 feet

verifiable_claims.claim: Two witnesses in Santa Fe on 23 Sept 1948 gave contradictory descriptions of the same object - one saw a flat white stationary disc, the other a silvery oblong object moving at 700-800 MPH

verifiable_claims.claim: An F-61 night fighter's airborne radar detected an unknown object over Fukuoka, Japan on 15 Oct 1948 that appeared to know the F-61's location and could accelerate out of radar range
